terra.problem: The claim that nobody opens a first prayer with 'How long' is an unsupported absolute. The words suggest Habakkuk has been calling for help, but they do not establish a rule about everyone’s first prayer.
The picture of people boxed in on every side with nowhere to move goes beyond Habakkuk’s statement that the wicked hem in the righteous.
The oven-timer joke makes the LORD’s warning the comparison’s punchline, rather than keeping the humor on the human side.
The dwellings are not the Chaldeans’ own, but the text does not say they were never theirs.
The passage does not say the homes were never theirs; it says the dwellings are not their own.
The text says the Chaldeans derive justice and sovereignty from themselves. It does not say they never look to anyone else for what is right.
Adding that their justice comes from nowhere else goes beyond the text’s statement that they derive it from themselves.
Saying the horses beat leopards turns the comparison into a claim about an actual race.
The verse pictures a vulture swooping down, but it does not say there was no slow circle.
The text says the Chaldeans build siege ramps to seize fortresses; it does not say they build the ramps over the walls.

The claim that nobody worships what they laugh at is an unsupported generalization. The passage says the Chaldeans scorn rulers and that their own strength is their god, without giving that explanation.
